cases.sentence: Я умираю от ___, не знаю, что мне делать.
cases.explain: The preposition «от» (from, out of) always takes the genitive, so скука becomes скуки.

cases.sentence: В ваших жилах течет русалочья ___, будьте же русалкой!
cases.explain: Кровь is the subject of the verb течёт (flows), and the subject stands in the nominative.

cases.sentence: Здесь в ___ есть мой собственный стол.
cases.explain: «В» meaning location (where, not where to) takes the prepositional: в доме.

cases.sentence: На этом ___ жили лебеди, гуси, утки.
cases.explain: «На» indicating a place where something happens (no motion) governs the prepositional case.
Допрос is the direct object of сделать; as an inanimate masculine noun its accusative looks like the nominative.
The short passive participle занята takes the instrumental for the thing doing the covering.

cases.sentence: На каждый двор приходилось по три ___.
cases.explain: The numerals два, три and четыре are followed by the genitive singular, so три лошади.
The verb противоречить (to contradict) governs the dative case of the person contradicted.

cases.sentence: Я питаю к ___ не только благоговение, но и родственные чувства.
cases.explain: The preposition «к» (towards) always takes the dative: к науке.

cases.sentence: Мой покойный отец купил это имение в приданое для моей ___.
cases.explain: The preposition «для» (for the benefit of) requires the genitive, hence для сестры.

reading.ru: Без четверти час.
reading.question: What time is it when Voynitsky mentions the meeting the professor has called?
reading.correct: A quarter to one
reading.explain: Voynitsky looks at his watch and says it is a quarter to one; the professor asked everyone to gather at one o'clock.

reading.ru: Я умираю от скуки, не знаю, что мне делать.
reading.question: How does Elena Andreevna describe her own state at the start of the act?
options: She is dying of boredom and does not know what to do
She is worried about her husband's health
She is happy to be in the country
reading.correct: She is dying of boredom and does not know what to do
reading.explain: Elena complains of boredom, which is why Sonya starts suggesting things she could do.

reading.ru: Хозяйством занимайся, учи, лечи.
reading.question: What does Sonya suggest Elena could do with herself?
options: Run the household, teach and treat the sick
Learn to play the piano again
Go back to Petersburg for the winter
reading.correct: Run the household, teach and treat the sick
reading.explain: Sonya lists practical country occupations, but Elena answers that she cannot and is not interested.

reading.ru: Ты колдунья, должно быть.
reading.question: What does Sonya jokingly conclude about Elena after noting how often the doctor now visits?
options: That she must be a witch
That she must be in love with Uncle Vanya
That she must be planning to leave
reading.correct: That she must be a witch
reading.explain: Astrov used to come once a month but now comes every day, so Sonya teases that Elena has bewitched him.

reading.ru: В знак мира и согласия я принесу сейчас букет роз; еще утром для вас приготовил...
reading.question: What does Voynitsky go to fetch as a token of peace after upsetting Elena?
options: A bouquet of roses he prepared in the morning
A bottle of wine from the cellar
The account books of the estate
A shawl for the cold evening
reading.correct: A bouquet of roses he prepared in the morning
reading.explain: He apologises and leaves to bring the autumn roses he had already picked for her.

reading.ru: Вот уже и сентябрь.
reading.question: What time of year is it in this act?
reading.correct: September, the beginning of autumn
reading.explain: Elena looks out of the window and remarks that September has come and wonders how they will get through the winter.

reading.ru: Я некрасива.
reading.question: What does Sonya say about her own appearance when she talks with Elena?
options: That she looks like her mother
That she has grown thin from work
That she does not care how she looks
reading.correct: That she is not beautiful
reading.explain: Elena answers by praising her hair, which Sonya says is what people always tell a plain woman.

reading.ru: И вся прислуга знает, что я его люблю.
reading.question: Who, according to Sonya, already knows that she loves Astrov?
options: All the servants in the house
reading.correct: All the servants in the house
reading.explain: She admits she has lost all pride: she confessed to Uncle Vanya and the whole household knows.

reading.ru: Позволь, я поговорю с ним...
reading.question: What does Elena offer to do to help Sonya?
options: Speak to Astrov herself and find out the truth
Write to Astrov on Sonya's behalf
Ask the professor to invite Astrov to stay
reading.correct: Speak to Astrov herself and find out the truth
reading.explain: Elena proposes to question the doctor cautiously, by hints, so that he will not notice.

reading.ru: Я скажу, что ты хочешь видеть его чертежи...
reading.question: What pretext is used to bring Astrov into the drawing room?
options: That Elena wants to see his drawings
That the professor has asked for him
That someone in the village is ill
That Sonya wants to say goodbye
reading.correct: That Elena wants to see his drawings
reading.explain: Astrov had offered to show his maps, so Sonya goes to say that Elena wishes to see them.

reading.ru: Нет ничего хуже, когда знаешь чужую тайну и не можешь помочь.
reading.question: What does Elena say once she is left alone?
options: That nothing is worse than knowing someone else's secret and being unable to help
That she has never liked Sonya
That she will tell her husband everything
That country life has made her cruel
reading.correct: That nothing is worse than knowing someone else's secret and being unable to help
reading.explain: Alone, she reflects on Sonya's hopeless love and on her own growing attraction to Astrov.

reading.ru: Картина нашего уезда, каким он был 50 лет назад.
reading.question: What does the first section of Astrov's map show?
options: The district as it was fifty years ago
A plan of the professor's estate
The roads he travels as a doctor
A design for a new forest he wants to plant
reading.correct: The district as it was fifty years ago
reading.explain: In that first picture half the whole area is under forest, with elk, wild goats, swans and geese.

reading.ru: Коз уже нет, но лоси есть.
reading.question: In the picture of twenty-five years ago, what has already changed?
options: The wild goats are gone, though elk remain
The elk are gone, though goats remain
The lake has dried up completely
reading.correct: The wild goats are gone, though elk remain
reading.explain: By then only a third of the area is forest and the green and blue colours are already paler.

reading.ru: Разрушено уже почти все, но взамен не создано еще ничего.
reading.question: How does Astrov sum up what has happened to the district?
options: Almost everything has been destroyed and nothing created in its place
The land is poorer but the people are healthier
Factories and railways have replaced the forests
The decline can still be stopped within a year
reading.correct: Almost everything has been destroyed and nothing created in its place
reading.explain: He blames degeneration caused by ignorance and the hopeless struggle for existence, not by real progress.

reading.ru: Да, я ее уважаю.
reading.question: What is Astrov's first answer when Elena asks whether he likes Sonya?
reading.correct: That he respects her
reading.explain: When Elena presses further and asks whether he likes Sonya as a woman, he answers no.

reading.ru: Вы не любите ее, по глазам вижу...
reading.question: How does Elena say she can tell that Astrov does not love Sonya?
options: She can see it in his eyes
He said so to the professor
He never comes to the house
reading.correct: She can see it in his eyes
reading.explain: She therefore asks him to stop coming to the house, since Sonya is suffering.

reading.ru: Хищница милая, не смотрите на меня так, я старый воробей...
reading.question: What does Astrov call Elena when he sees through her questioning?
reading.correct: A sweet beast of prey
reading.explain: He calls her a predator and a pretty polecat who needs victims, and admits he is beaten.

reading.ru: Приезжай завтра в лесничество... часам к двум...
reading.question: Where does Astrov ask Elena to meet him the next day?
options: At the forest station at about two o'clock
In town, at the doctor's own house
reading.correct: At the forest station at about two o'clock
reading.explain: He kisses her and asks where they can meet, naming the forestry station at around two.

reading.ru: Я, Helene, все видел, все...
reading.question: What does Voynitsky say to Elena after he walks in with the roses?
options: That he will tell the professor at once
That he does not believe his own eyes
reading.correct: That he saw everything
reading.explain: He comes in with the bouquet just as Astrov kisses Elena, and afterwards wipes his face and admits he saw it all.

reading.ru: Двадцать шесть громадных комнат, разбредутся все, и никого никогда не найдешь.
reading.question: What does Serebryakov complain about the house?
options: It has twenty-six huge rooms and everyone gets lost in it
It is too small for the whole family
It is cold and the stoves smoke
It is falling down and needs repairs
reading.correct: It has twenty-six huge rooms and everyone gets lost in it
reading.explain: He calls the house a labyrinth and says country life feels to him like life on an alien planet.

reading.ru: Я предлагаю продать имение.
reading.question: What is the proposal Serebryakov gathers the family to announce?
options: To rent the estate to Telegin
To move Uncle Vanya into the lodge
reading.correct: To sell the estate
reading.explain: He wants to convert the money into interest-bearing securities that would yield four to five percent.

reading.ru: Это имение было куплено по тогдашнему времени за девяносто пять тысяч.
reading.question: How much was the estate bought for, according to Voynitsky?
reading.correct: Ninety-five thousand
reading.explain: His father paid only seventy thousand of it, and Voynitsky worked for ten years to pay off the remaining twenty-five thousand.

reading.ru: Если бы я жил нормально, то из меня мог бы выйти Шопенгауэр, Достоевский...
reading.question: Who does Voynitsky claim he might have become if his life had been normal?
reading.correct: A Schopenhauer or a Dostoevsky
reading.explain: In his despair he insists he is talented and clever and that Serebryakov ruined his life.

reading.ru: За сценой выстрел; слышно, как вскрикивает Елена Андреевна; Соня вздрагивает.
reading.question: What happens offstage while Sonya is clinging to the nurse?
options: A shot is fired and Elena screams
A window is broken by the wind
reading.correct: A shot is fired and Elena screams
reading.explain: The stage direction gives the shot offstage, after which Serebryakov runs in shouting that Voynitsky has gone mad.

reading.ru: Опять промах?!
reading.question: What is the result when Voynitsky fires at Serebryakov on stage?
options: He wounds him in the arm
He shoots at the ceiling on purpose
reading.correct: He misses him
reading.explain: After firing he cries that he missed again, throws the revolver on the floor and collapses onto a chair.

reading.ru: Погогочут гусаки - и перестанут...
reading.question: How does the nurse Marina describe the family's quarrelling?
options: The ganders will cackle a while and then stop
It will end in disaster before evening
It is all the professor's wife's fault
It happens every autumn in this house
reading.correct: The ganders will cackle a while and then stop
reading.explain: Marina strokes Sonya's head, promises her lime-flower tea, and dismisses the row as geese honking.

highlight.question: Which sentence says how the doctor's visits to the house have changed?
sentences: А вот я так не понимаю, как это не идти и не учить.
Погоди, и ты привыкнешь.
Не скучай, родная.
Ты скучаешь, не находишь себе места, а скука и праздность заразительны.
Смотри: дядя Ваня ничего не делает и только ходит за тобою, как тень, я оставила свои дела и прибежала к тебе, чтобы поговорить.
Обленилась, не могу!
Доктор Михаил Львович прежде бывал у нас очень редко, раз в месяц, упросить его было трудно, а теперь он ездит сюда каждый день, бросил и свои леса и медицину.
Ты колдунья, должно быть.
highlight.explain: Sonya contrasts the doctor's rare monthly visits in the past with his daily visits now.

highlight.question: Which sentence urges Elena to fall in love and plunge headlong into the pool?
sentences: Что томитесь?
Ну, дорогая моя, роскошь, будьте умницей!
В ваших жилах течет русалочья кровь, будьте же русалкой!
Дайте себе волю хоть раз в жизни, влюбитесь поскорее в какого-нибудь водяного по самые уши - и бултых с головой в омут, чтобы герр профессор и все мы только руками развели!
highlight.explain: The last sentence is the one that tells her to let herself go and dive into the whirlpool.

highlight.question: Which sentence tells us how long Sonya has been in love with Astrov?
sentences: Я его люблю уже шесть лет, люблю больше, чем свою мать; я каждую минуту слышу его, чувствую пожатие его руки; и я смотрю на дверь, жду, мне все кажется, что он сейчас войдет.
И вот, ты видишь, я все прихожу к тебе, чтобы поговорить о нем.
Теперь он бывает здесь каждый день, не смотрит на меня, не видит...
Это такое страдание!
У меня нет никакой надежды, нет, нет!
highlight.explain: Only the first sentence gives the length of time, six years.

highlight.question: Which sentence compares Astrov's arrival to a bright moon rising in the darkness?
sentences: Я понимаю эту бедную девочку.

Среди отчаянной скуки, когда вместо людей кругом бродят какие-то серые пятна, слышатся одни пошлости, когда только и знают, что едят, пьют, спят, иногда приезжает он, не похожий на других, красивый, интересный, увлекательный, точно среди потемок восходит месяц ясный...
Поддаться обаянию такого человека, забыться...
Кажется, я сама увлеклась немножко.
Да, мне без него скучно, я вот улыбаюсь, когда думаю о нем...
highlight.explain: The long second sentence ends with the image of a clear moon rising among the shadows.

highlight.question: Which sentence says how much of the district was still under forest twenty-five years ago?
sentences: Теперь посмотрим ниже.
То, что было двадцать пять лет назад.
Тут уж под лесом только одна треть всей площади.
Коз уже нет, но лоси есть.
Зеленая и голубая краски уже бледнее.
highlight.explain: Astrov states that by then only one third of the whole area was forest.

highlight.question: Which sentence says that selling the forest is a measure that cannot be used every year?
sentences: Продолжать жить в деревне мне невозможно.
Мы для деревни не созданы.
Жить же в городе на те средства, какие мы получаем от этого имения, невозможно.
Если продать, положим, лес, то эта мера экстраординарная, которою нельзя пользоваться ежегодно.
Нужно изыскать такие меры, которые гарантировали бы нам постоянную, более или менее определенную цифру дохода.
highlight.explain: Serebryakov calls a sale of the forest an extraordinary measure that cannot be repeated yearly.

highlight.question: Which sentence gives the original purchase price of the estate?
sentences: Это имение было куплено по тогдашнему времени за девяносто пять тысяч.
Отец уплатил только семьдесят, и осталось долгу двадцать пять тысяч.
Теперь слушайте...
Имение это не было бы куплено, если бы я не отказался от наследства в пользу сестры, которую горячо любил.
Мало того, я десять лет работал, как вол, и выплатил весь долг...
highlight.explain: The first sentence names ninety-five thousand as the price at the time.

highlight.question: Which sentence recalls Uncle Vanya and the grandmother translating books at night for the professor?
sentences: Надо быть милосердным, папа!
Я и дядя Ваня так несчастны!
Вспомни, когда ты был помоложе, дядя Ваня и бабушка по ночам переводили для тебя книги, переписывали твои бумаги... все ночи, все ночи!
Я и дядя Ваня работали без отдыха, боялись потратить на себя копейку и всё посылали тебе...
Мы не ели даром хлеба!
highlight.explain: Sonya reminds her father of the nights her uncle and grandmother spent translating and copying for him.
